answer: Correlation penalties: when many accounts answer in lockstep, share timing, or echo phrasing, the ledger treats that overlap as a signal of one operator and splits a single reward among the whole cluster. A sybil farm then grows like a vine on one root, so cutting the root starves every shoot. To profit, an attacker must make each fake behave independently, like a lone cedar, which costs separate compute, distinct writing, and staggered schedules per identity, erasing the gain from multiplying accounts.
